RQ1.rationale: The paper presents a general CubeSat reference model for mission/system modeling, but EPS is only a power-subsystem block and the method assumes intermediate space/MBSE/SysML knowledge rather than minimal behavioral knowledge.

RQ2.rationale: The paper claims reuse, productivity, traceability, interoperability, and reliability-requirement decomposition benefits from MBSE/CRM use, but not EPS-specific outcomes and not with quantitative evidence.

RQ3.rationale: The paper provides pre-physical system/model V&V through viewpoints, representative mission population, requirements traces, and mission modeling, but no EPS-specific verification procedure.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Part of the recurring INCOSE SSWG CubeSat Reference Model lineage. The paper cites prior SSWG work on RAX scenarios, integrated MBSE simulation, trade studies, CRM interim status papers, development/distribution, and CubeSat behavior modeling. This extraction uses only claims and details in this paper.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.minimal_or_excluded_modeling: The CRM is not a specific mission design. toolchain_interoperability_lifecycle_con.syntax_semantic_continuity_evidence: The paper states an independent review team will validate compliance with accepted SysML modeling guidelines and OMG review/approval will validate specification qualification. newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.rationale: The paper discusses low-cost university CubeSat teams and COTS components but does not provide an agile, distributed, NewSpace, or rapid-iteration process.
newspace_agile_distributed_rapid_iterati.evidence: Section 1: The CubeSat Project was established for the university community to design, build, and launch satellites using mostly off-the-shelf components.

RQ1: The CRM provides a general high-abstraction CubeSat mission/domain reference model spanning stakeholders, external environment/constraints, space and ground segments, logical subsystems, requirements, use cases, measures, and V&V packages.
Mission teams can populate mission-specific needs, objectives, constraints, measures, use cases, requirements, V&V approach, and physical architecture from the CRM.
EPS is not modeled in detail; only a generic logical Power Subsystem is included.
The method does not minimize behavioral/domain knowledge fully because it assumes intermediate space mission, MBSE, and SysML knowledge plus SME guidance.
RQ2: Claimed outcomes include reuse/flexibility, productivity/efficiency, traceability, mission-assurance/V&V facilitation, COTS tool interoperability, communication alignment, and future reference-model retrieval.
Reliability appears as an example of non-functional requirement decomposition into redundancy-related lower-level requirements, not as measured reliability evidence.

Reproducibility and integrability are conceptual: planned CRM delivery/OMG specification and COTS interface claims exist, but no model files, tool details, interface mechanisms, metrics, or integration results are provided.
RQ3: The paper integrates V&V into the system/reference model using validation/verification packages, viewpoints, requirements/use-case/technical-measure traces, representative mission population, V&V scenarios, and mission modeling.
Pre-physical verification is described for the CRM and mission-specific CubeSat model, but not at EPS level.
Test and evaluation augmentation is explicitly future work; no EPS verification procedure, automated test, SIL/HIL, flat-sat, environmental test, or flight result is reported.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: Further research is needed to augment the CRM with other models for CubeSat test and evaluation.
The CRM is at least three levels of abstraction away from any physical instantiation.
Use assumes intermediate understanding of space mission analysis/design, MBSE, and SysML, with SME guidance.
Figure 4 relationships are illustrative not prescriptive.
The CRM activity is ongoing and expected to continue into the foreseeable future.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No EPS-specific architecture, components, modes, power budgets, requirements, or verification procedures are presented.
No named SysML tool, model version, repository, downloadable model files, data-exchange mechanism, or COTS interface details are provided.
No quantitative metrics, baseline comparison, stakeholder evaluation, independent validation results, integration/test results, or flight/operational evidence support outcomes.
No formal lifecycle gate mapping, configuration/change-control process, versioning convention, or ROI evidence is reported.
Several strong value claims, especially productivity and absence of negative impacts, are asserted rather than evidenced.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: A CubeSat is a low-cost standardized nanosatellite.
Provide a CubeSat Reference Model (CRM) for CubeSat teams to use as the starting point for developing mission-specific CubeSat models.
Even though it is at least three levels of abstraction away from any physical instantiation, it still provides valuable assistance to the Mission-specific CubeSat development teams.
The CRM is intended to be used by university project teams designing space missions utilizing the CubeSat form-factor.

The model is being developed assuming that the members of the team have an intermediate-level understanding of space mission analysis and design, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), Systems Modeling Language (SysML), and that their work is being guided by subject matter experts.
Generate, regulate, store, and distribute power to the spacecraft.
The enterprise, segment, and subsystems packages contain behaviors, structures, validation, and verification packages.
Segment requirements are derived from mission requirements and trace to mission use cases.
The first step is taking the CRM and populating the mission-specific enterprise needs, objectives, constraints, and measures of effectiveness to create a mission-specific logical architecture.
The CRM will be populated with a representative mission, and then the viewpoints will provide the objective evidence for verification.
